title: EXPRESS: Expanding Markets or Capturing Share? The Competitive Effects of Subscriptions on Spending in Restaurant Delivery
eligible_reason: Staggered subscription adoption, but estimated as a propensity-score-matched stacked DiD with cohort-by-customer-type-by-month time effects and a time-varying control (monthly grocery spend). Matching and stacked designs are excluded.
design_notes: Consumer Edge card-transaction panel of individuals; treatment = signing up for Postmates Unlimited (Sept 2017 - Aug 2018 cohorts), study period through July 2019. Each subscriber is matched one-to-one without replacement (propensity score on pre-treatment spending at focal and competing firms, exact match on tenure and calendar time) to a non-subscriber. Equation (1): Y_it = beta Post_it x Treat_i + phi_i + xi_{g(i),t} + theta Control_it + e_it, where xi is a fixed effect for adoption cohort x customer type (singlehomer / multihomer) x month and Control_it = total monthly grocery spend (time-varying). Table 2 main estimate: log(1+focal spend) = 0.644 (SE .044), N = 74,448; Table 6 gives alternatives (CEM matching, unmatched 7,013,646 obs, IHS, levels, exclude month 0). All variants keep the cohort-by-type time fixed effects (stacked/matched structure) and the grocery-spend control, and use customer-clustered SEs. The paper states that a plain TWFE without cohort-specific time effects fails to deliver parallel pre-trends (Web Appendix 3.1).
screener_notes: Not eligible: matching-based stacked DiD with a time-varying control; no unstacked TWFE or event-study specification is reported in the main text. A no-matching variant exists (Table 6 analysis 3) but keeps cohort-by-type-by-time FE and the grocery control. Data supplied by Consumer Edge under license; synthetic data and code deposited in JMR Dataverse doi 10.7910/DVN/QZYBRG (stated as unpublished at time of manuscript).
data_note: Real data not public; Dataverse deposit holds synthetic data.
